key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the identification of the accused by PW1 in the Court Room and the recovery of Rs.1 lakh each from the accused as key evidence, but found these insufficient for conviction due to lack of proper procedural compliance.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of PW1, the eye-witness, as having contradictions in his FIR and deposition, and noted that he did not disclose any description of the accused prior to the trial, which raised doubts about his ability to identify the accused accurately.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 08.05.2001 (post mortem conducted on 08.05.2001), Trial judgment: 01.04.2011, High Court decision: 01.04.2011, Supreme Court decision: 11.07.2022
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Ms. Roohina Dua, Ms. Mansi Gupta, Sangram Saron, Shree Pal Singh; Counsel for the State: Ms. Richa Kapoor, Ms. Jaspreet Gogia, Ms. Aishwarya Mishra, Kunal Anand
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Non-conduct of Test Identification Parade (TIP) noted as a procedural lapse
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted under Sections 302 r/w 34 and 392 IPC; High Court: Confirmed conviction; Supreme Court: Quashed and set aside conviction, acquitted accused
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused were convicted based on the identification of the accused by PW1, the eye-witness, and the recovery of Rs.1 lakh each from the accused, which was alleged to be the looted amount. They also claimed that the complainant and the deceased were carrying Rs.5 lakhs in the dicky of the scooter.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the conviction was solely based on the identification of the accused by PW1 in court for the first time without conducting a Test Identification Parade (TIP), which is a critical flaw. They also contended that the prosecution failed to prove the presence of Rs.5 lakhs in the scooter and that the recovered amount was not the looted amount.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the identification of the accused for the first time in court without a TIP is not sufficient for conviction, and that the prosecution must establish the connection between the recovered amount and the alleged loot.
precedent_relied_upon: Malkhansingh and Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2003) 5 SCC 746; Md. Kalam v. State of Rajasthan (2008) 11 SCC 352
